title: Chapter 37: The Curse Arts User’s Identity
content:
Chapter 37:

The Curse Arts User’s True Identity

“Sister and you, Subaru… seem to be getting along quite well.”

When they met up at the designated spot, those were the first words Rem said to the two of them.

Her gaze was directed between them, specifically where Ram was tugging at Subaru’s sleeve. Subaru, the person in question, thought that if you just cropped that part, it might indeed look like a somewhat suggestive scene.

Laughing off Rem’s hasty conclusion, Subaru pointed at the scene in question,

“There’s no hidden meaning, alright? It’s purely a case of Ram-chi losing her patience because I was taking too long. Sorry to keep you waiting.”

He lightly shook his sleeve, removing her fingers, and apologized to Rem for keeping her waiting. Even so, Rem’s gaze seemed to remain somewhat cold, but when Ram slid over to stand next to her, she dropped the look.

I see, looking at it now that I have some mental leeway, Rem’s mentality is actually full of flaws despite her unflappable appearance. Especially when it comes to Ram, her precarious sister complex is laid bare for all to see.

“Sister…”

“Barusu says so too, Rem. There is no hidden meaning, is there?”

Ram casually dismissed her sister’s clinging tone with a composed face. Staring intently at her sister who shared the exact same face, Rem suddenly narrowed her eyes as if realizing something,

“Sister, did you perhaps use clairvoyance?”

“Indeed.”

“…Even after Rem told you to stop.”

“If it’s necessary, Ram will do it. Saying anything more is a waste of breath, Rem.”

“When you two talk in your own little world, I feel left out and might cry. Let me join in and have a pleasant chat, won’t ya!”

The serious Rem, Ram who brushed her off, and Subaru who jokingly cut in. The two of them, Rem in particular, shot a sharp glare at Subaru’s attitude.

The exact reason was unclear, but he seemed to have triggered Rem’s wariness quite significantly. Conversely, he felt like he was gaining favor with Ram, making him realize anew just how difficult these twins were to handle.

At this rate, the atmosphere was heading straight for a 

BAD

 end.

He wanted to raise Rem’s affection rating somehow, but he didn’t even have a clue where to start.

For the time being,

“A-A-Anyway, you know. Let’s not be so bloodthirsty and try to have some fun. I’ll do whatever it takes for our original objective, even carry the luggage.”

Rolling his shoulders and twisting his waist, he put on a show of being eager to work.

Some of the smaller groceries were likely already in the packages Rem and Ram were carrying. If Ram was right, Subaru’s role was supposed to be the heavy lifting that required a man’s strength.

With that in mind, he cast his gaze behind the twins, and immediately regretted it.

Because he spotted something resembling a barrel sitting there boldly, looking large enough to require a full embrace to carry.

“…Don’t you think there’s a limit to these things?”

“Seven times.”

“Huh?”

As Subaru dropped his voice, imagining diagonal lines of despair drawn across his face, Rem’s lips suddenly muttered a mysterious number. In response to Subaru tilting his head in confusion, Rem looked at him with testing eyes,

“Rem plans to take breaks along the way to match your pace, Subaru. Her estimate is seven times.”

At her bowing with her usual polite yet insolent attitude, Subaru thought about the distance back to the mansion. Roughly a twenty-minute walk. In a straight line, it was less than three kilometers, but Subaru was keenly aware of his own lack of stamina.

Then, he silently walked up to the barrel and gently tested its weight. Perhaps it was a paper tiger, all bark and no bite. Such pathetic hopes were easily crushed by the heavy weight that dug straight into his lower back.

Carrying this, for three kilometers, resting seven times—.

He twisted his waist, did some knee bends on the spot, gave his back a big stretch, and said,

“I’ll do my best to keep it under ten.”

Far from feeling rebellious at being provoked about needing seven breaks, he actually kind of liked that he was setting up a safety net by proposing an even higher number.

“By the way, Ram estimates you’ll rest thirteen times.”

“You guys are certainly fair when it comes to not letting personal feelings affect whether your evaluations are strict or lenient.”

Even with the slight difference in their affection levels, it still felt like Rem was evaluating him slightly better.

That in itself was a situation that made him want to tilt his head in confusion.

※※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※

It was past evening, with the sun dipping low, when the three of them finally arrived back at the mansion.

Defeated by the weight of the load, collapsing repeatedly, Subaru had proposed taking a break roughly twelve times along the way. His biceps were already screaming from the built-up lactic acid, and the spasm-like trembling in his lower legs showed no signs of stopping.

He easily lost to Rem’s estimate, and the only thing that kept him walking this far was his thin pride of refusing to yield to Ram’s malice.

“We made it… we made it… Well done, me! GJ! Seriously, GJ.”

“Sister, sister, Subaru is crawling on the ground, overjoyed.”

“Rem, Rem, Barusu is prostrating himself on the ground like a dog, deeply moved.”

“Shut up, before you hurl insults, praise me for actually pulling it off first! I’m naïve and delicate, so if you only use the stick, I’ll break easily. I’m from the Relaxed Education generation, so I haven’t experienced many 

setbacks!”

1

Especially since coming to this world, there had been way too much of the stick. Of course, he was aware he was also being given some pretty sweet carrots, but even taking that into consideration, wasn’t the stick a little too powerful?

Anyway,

“Yes, yes, good job.”

“Yes, yes, thanks.”

Giving Subaru her perfunctory thanks for his efforts, Rem effortlessly lifted the liquor barrel resting on the ground.

Subaru, whose personal record for the bench press was eighty kilograms, would have struggled to lift it above his shoulders even if he went all out. Yet Rem lifted an object of that weight with one hand, while holding smaller packages in the other.

At the very absurdity of the downright epic sight, Subaru couldn't help but smile,

“Was I even needed?”

“No? From the beginning, without Barusu, this is something Ram and Rem always did by ourselves anyway… as you can see.”

Ram had no intention of coddling the inner little boy within Subaru.

Watching Rem walk away with a steady stride that seemed like it needed its own SFX, Subaru fully realized just how meaningless his manual labor had been.

“Then why the hell did you make me do it…? Was it seriously just harassment? Come on, Senior, please stop hazing your junior.”

“Don’t you understand, Barusu? It was consideration, of course.”

“I don’t get it at all. Consideration for what?”

At Subaru’s question, Ram scoffed “Hah” through her nose, then shrugged and struck an exasperated pose,

“So you’re saying, Barusu, you wouldn’t mind Lady Emilia seeing you triumphantly returning with only a small bag holding a few spices, while Rem walks behind you carrying a massive liquor barrel?”

“Seriously, Senior, I have no words for your consideration!”

He dropped to his knees, expressing his gratitude to Ram’s divine visage.

Making a girl smaller than him carry a massive load while he strutted back with just a shopping bag looking smug—what kind of hellish picture was that?

Even before Emilia saw him, just looking at himself in the mirror would surely plunge him into despair. Having his flimsy ‘manliness points’ worn down was a walk in the park compared to that.

Just then,

“Sister, Master Roswaal is—”

Rem, who had gone ahead with the luggage, returned to the two exchanging words in front of the entrance. It was Ram who reacted at high speed to her uttering the lord of the mansion’s name.

Showing just how much vitality that name brought her, Ram completely swept away the slightly listless atmosphere she normally carried, aligned herself next to her sister with brisk movements, and fixed her appearance as she walked. Then,

“What are you doing, Barusu. Do you plan to keep Master Roswaal waiting?”

“I can’t understand what you guys communicate through your twin telepathy. Wait, what, does this mean ‘servants assemble’ or something?”

Looked at as if he were a slow-witted child, Subaru scratched his head and hurriedly followed the two. Along the way, copying Ram, he hastily straightened his appearance, and when he opened the mansion’s entrance doors,

“Aha~a, so you two were together. That saves me the trouble.”

Roswaal, the lord of the mansion, was waiting for the three of them with open arms.

Long indigo hair, and blue and yellow heterochromia. A handsome man wearing a slovenly, relaxed smile—but right now, his atmosphere was different from usual.

“Are you dressed for going out?”

“Right on the mark. No~o, I don’t particularly care either, you see~. If I wear my usual attire, there are a~always those who get jealous, so I relu~uctantly, unavo~oidably, have to wear formal clothes like thi~is.”

The man who usually preferred outfits brimming with excessive playfulness—with ridiculously large collars, geometric patterns, and colors that seemed to blend into the background—was currently dressed in proper attire, similar to when they first met.

Seeing Roswaal’s outfit, two possibilities came to Subaru’s mind.

And,

“Do we have a guest?”

“Are you going out?”

The possibilities Subaru thought of were simultaneously spoken by the twins.

At the questions from his servants, Roswaal offered a wry smile,

“Ram is correct, I am going out. Some ra~ather troublesome news has come in~. I’m going to see Garfiel to confirm it. I don’t plan to be late, though~.”

It was a name he’d never heard before, and he didn’t even know if it referred to a person or a place.

But, following the twins who nodded as if they understood everything just from that, Subaru also nodded at Roswaal’s words without raising any objections.

He nodded magnanimously at the attitude of the three,

“So~o, that’s why I’ll be away from the mansion for a bit. Regardless, I don’t think I’ll be back tonight—so Ram, Rem. I leave things in your ha~ands.”

“Yes, if that is your order.”

“Yes, even at the cost of my life.”

He acknowledged the two who nodded without hesitation with just his eyes, and then his heterochromic gaze fixed on Subaru. Feeling slightly overwhelmed by that gleam, Subaru shifted uncomfortably,

“Sorry, but I haven’t sworn loyalty to the point of giving my life yet~, y’know?”

“That’s pe~erfectly fine. It’d be heavy and unse~ettling if you suddenly swore something like that, anyway. But we~ell, I’ll leave things to you too, Subaru.”

Patting his shoulder, Roswaal closed one eye, reflecting Subaru only in his yellow one,

“I smell something fishy. Don’t worry about me… but please, make absolu~utely sure you take care of Lady Emilia, alri~ight?”

“—Yeah, you can seriously count on me for that.”

He didn’t need to be told.

Subaru didn’t know to what extent Roswaal found the situation suspicious. He didn’t know, but Subaru responded clearly all the same.

—An unprecedented development.

This development meant exactly that: a change had occurred in the world due to the actions Subaru had taken.

Receiving Subaru’s nod, Roswaal nodded in satisfaction.

Then, he left a word or two with his loyal twin retainers,

“We~ell then, I’ll be off. Let us pray that nothing happens, shall we~.”

Muttering that in a somewhat low voice, Roswaal’s back disappeared beyond the entrance.

Subaru suddenly saw off his retreating back with a bow, then,

“Wait, I just realized, you two aren’t going with him. Plus, there was no sign of a carriage or anything outside… is he walking?”

In response to Subaru’s question, the twins simultaneously harbored a look of exasperation in their eyes,

“Because there’s no point in us going. We’d only be a hindrance.”

“You can’t fly through the sky on loyalty alone. And people would see up our skirts.”

“Hey hey, you guys just dropped a whole bunch of words I can’t ignore…”

To Subaru, they were a devastating fighting force on par with Elsa, but the two of them clearly recognized their own lack of power. Furthermore, if he believed Ram’s statement,

“Whoa, seriously…”

He pushed open the entrance doors where Roswaal had disappeared, confirming that the lord was nowhere to be seen outside. Then, turning his gaze toward the sky and scanning for a moment, he could barely make out a bean-sized shadow flapping a cape far off in the direction of the sunset. There was no mistaking it; that was Roswaal flying solo.

“He can fly through the sky…? Can you do that with Yin magic too?”

“You can if you can handle Wind, Fire, and Earth magic appropriately.”

At Ram’s words, Subaru covered his face at how far off the day that would become reality was.

Subaru’s lack of magical talent had already been firmly guaranteed by both a court mage and a spirit.

Who knew when the day would come that he could fly freely through the sky?

Putting aside such sentiments,

“Even without Master Roswaal, our duties remain the same. In fact, because Master Roswaal isn’t here, we must perform them flawlessly.”

“What an honor-student answer. But alright, let’s get to it.”

While nodding at Rem as she began taking charge, Subaru’s brain was spinning rapidly.

Once again, a change had come about in the situation.

And it was a change that clearly foreshadowed an attack. The twins were likely also fired up, thinking they needed to put even more effort into guarding the mansion, but Subaru, who knew for sure that an attack was coming, was far from calm.

The curse arts user’s true identity—he needed to grasp it as quickly as possible.

There was no doubt that the enemy’s actions had sped up, and today’s visit to the village was likely the trigger.

In other words, Subaru’s deduction was correct, and the assassin was undoubtedly hiding among them.

※※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※ ※

“So with that being said, it’s the long-awaited Beako Time.”

Pushing open the door, he stepped into the Forbidden Library.

At his overly familiar way of barging in, Beatrice, who was sitting on a stepladder reading a book, dramatically dropped her shoulders,

“You’re about the only one who breaches Betty’s Door Crossing so easily, in fact. How do you even do it, I wonder?”

“Intuition, just intuition. My sixth sense whispers to me.”

Closing the door behind him, he stepped inside and headed toward Beatrice. She watched Subaru approach with a look of profound disgust, but perhaps because she saw a trace of seriousness mixed in his expression, she suddenly narrowed her eyes,

“Your expression is different again compared to half a day ago, I suppose. You’re a busy one.”

“I’d like to take it easy for a bit too, y’know. But it seems this world is busy enough not to let me do that.”

An ordinary person could only barely keep up with changes in situations falling out of the blue, one after the other.

While fumbling forward dealing with this, that, and the other, it wasn’t uncommon for the situation to become completely deadlocked.

In that regard, he was cornered in the current situation. But on the other hand, he had the confidence that he was also cornering the enemy.

“There’s something I need you to confirm. I finished cleaning the bath at super express speed to get here.”

“If the bath had a higher priority, it doesn’t seem like a very important matter, in fact.”

“It wasn’t so much the bath having priority as it was managing Rem’s affection level… well, never mind that.”

Cleaning the vast bathhouse was backbreaking work. Even now that he was somewhat used to it, it was still heavy labor that left his entire body sluggish. Precisely because of that, Rem’s reaction if he slacked off was terrifying.

Especially since, towards a Subaru who was getting close with her sister, her affection level in this loop wasn’t very high to begin with.

Even if he found the curse arts user, if Rem’s affection was low and he entered a 

BAD

 route, Subaru wouldn’t be able to rest in peace.

Having to deal with two types of threats at once, Subaru felt like a two-timing man walking a tightrope.

Though he doubted there were many two-timing situations where messing up flag management led to immediate death.

“Besides, it’s not exactly that kind of sexy topic.”

“Your conversation is wandering again… So, what business do you have with Betty, I wonder?”

“Yeah, about that…”

For the time being, in front of Beatrice, who seemed willing to listen, Subaru pondered for a moment. Unsure of how to broach the subject, he gave a single nod,

“I think I might be cursed a little, could you check for me?”

“…What are you talking about, I wonder?”

“I think I might be cursed a little, could you check for me?”

“Who told you to say the exact same thing twice, I suppose! It’s only been half a day since the details of curse arts users were explained to you, in fact! There’s a limit to how easily influenced you can be…”

Perhaps thinking it was Subaru’s paranoia, Beatrice yelled at him and approached, slamming her book shut roughly. But halfway there, her momentum died down, and the emotion coloring her adorable face was replaced by suspicion, and then, certainty.

Stopping in her tracks, Beatrice looked up at Subaru with dubious eyes,

“There’s the presence of a spell rite… You really are cursed, in fact.”

“Seriously? Even though I kinda knew it would be, actually hearing it said out loud is a pretty big shock.”

Even prepared to suffer the effects of a curse, being flat-out told by someone else that he was indeed cursed still hit him hard.

Because it meant Subaru’s theory was affirmed, and it confirmed without a doubt that the assassin in question was hiding among those good-natured villagers.

“Can you tell what kind of curse it is?”

“That can’t be told just by looking at the spell rite, in fact. Betty doesn’t have deep knowledge about curses either, nor does she care to know, I suppose. However, nine times out of ten, it’s the kind that takes your life, in fact.”

It wasn’t a threat or anything; Beatrice simply stated the fact matter-of-factly.

Subaru nodded quietly at her words. That the curse exhibited that kind of power was a fact he had already experienced firsthand.

Perhaps surprised by Subaru’s unwavering expression, Beatrice blinked her large eyes rapidly,

“You’ve got nerve, in fact. Aren’t you afraid of dying, I wonder?”

“Huh? Are you stupid? Dying is super scary, y’know? There aren’t many things in this world scarier than dying. I’d really like the people who say they’d rather be dead to say that 

after

 they actually die.”

That was the one absolute, undeniable truth Subaru had gained in this different world.

Death was absolute. Treating it lightly was unacceptable. And casually using it as a point of comparison was nothing more than thoughtless folly capable only by those who didn’t understand its true nature.

Because he knew that, because Subaru had tasted Death so many times, he had restarted the world and come back precisely so he wouldn’t have to experience a sensation worse than Death.

“So this time, I’m gonna be the one cutting through, Fate.”

Pointing a finger at the heavens, Subaru threw a declaration of war at that supernatural entity watching from who knows where.

Then, turning back to Beatrice,

“Alright then, I need you to quickly break the curse. We’re out of time.”

At the very least, he had to identify the culprit and launch an offensive before the enemy took action.

Subaru was eager, getting his first chance to strike first. Looking at him, Beatrice tilted her head,

“And why should Betty have to save your life, I wonder?”

“I figured you’d say something uncute like that, so I prepared a persuasion tactic. If I die, Puck will be sad.”

“…Bubby wouldn’t be all that emotionally disturbed just because one or two humans like you died, I suppose.”

“No, no, if I die, Emilia-tan will be devastated. And if Emilia-tan is devastated, Puck will take damage too. And then, what would become of your position when you could’ve prevented it but didn’t!”

“To resort to threats when you’re supposed to be begging for your life, it is beyond doubt that you’ve completely lost your mind, in fact!”

Beatrice stomped the ground in irritation, seemingly unable to come up with an effective counterargument.

She rode her irritation on a long sigh, convincing herself, and beckoned Subaru to come closer.

“You’re allowed to sweet-talk me just this once, I suppose. However, Betty will absolutely never get involved in any further exchanges with you from now on, in fact.”

“To be honest, I can’t promise you that either. Whenever I’m in trouble, I’ll definitely come running to you for help. I’ll gnaw on your shins until they’re dust, make soup out of them, and drink it.”

“Are you even aware that you’re the one in the position to be saved, I wonder?”

“I have a reputation for pushing my way through. I didn’t become a shut-in for nothing.”

As Subaru flashed a thumbs-up and a sparkling smile, Beatrice shook her head in resignation.

Then, she suddenly gathered white light in her palm and touched Subaru’s body.

“Now, the curse mark where the spell rite is engraved is going to be destroyed, in fact. It’s the exact spot the curse arts user touched directly, so you might want to use it as a reference, I suppose.”

“Ooh yeah, I’ve already laid the groundwork for that, don’t worry.”

Watching the glowing palm approach, Subaru checked his body once more.

The positions he let the suspects touch him were all different. The Youth-Restoring Hag was the only one who ignored his intentions and touched his butt, but if Beatrice’s hand went for his butt, he’d deal with it then.

Accepting the fact that the hag was the culprit, he would also condemn Beatrice’s sexual harassment.

Subaru’s expectations—

“—Huh?”

Were completely shattered by the unexpected location Beatrice’s palm touched.

He felt the warm light sink into his skin, slowly generating heat. What suddenly arose was a faint itch. It seemed to well up from the inside, seeping out, and finally,

“A black, mist…?”

Within Beatrice's glowing hand, it became a black mist and was directly grasped.

The itch vanished, and he understood that the extracted mist had been the cause of that sensation. And that mist, within Beatrice’s palm,

“How utterly repulsive, I suppose.”

Disappeared with a squelching sensation, as if being crushed.

Beatrice waved her hand, shaking off both the mist and the light from her palm. Noticing Subaru’s gaze watching her, she said,

“It’s done, in fact. You should be fine now, I suppose.”

Being told that, Subaru let out an involuntary deep breath.

He hadn’t realized he’d been holding his breath out of tension, but before mocking his own cowardice, there was something he had to ask right now.

“Hey, Beako.”

“That name…”

“The place your palm just touched, that’s definitely the spot the curse arts user touched, right?”

Interrupting her and asking again, Beatrice nodded at Subaru’s words.

With that nod, Subaru realized the true identity of the curse arts user culprit behind the whole series of events.

According to his original plan, taking action after identifying the culprit was supposed to wait until tomorrow.

He would consult with Ram, Rem, and the lord of the mansion, Roswaal, and then smoke out the curse arts user in the village to resolve the situation.

That was the vision Subaru had in mind, but—

“I gotta go, to the village—!”

He dashed out the door, even forgetting to leave words of gratitude for Beatrice.

Original objectives and everything else thrown aside, the only thing occupying Subaru’s mind as he ran was a barrage of curses at his utterly merciless fate.

“No matter where, no matter when… stop screwing with me!”

Loading all the anger he could muster into his shouts, Subaru ran.

He ran.
